facts.statement: Mioaetus is an extinct genus of accipitrids meaning "Miocene eagle".
facts.quote: Mioaetus (meaning "Miocene eagle") is an extinct genus of accipitrid from the Miocene of the Hammerschmiede clay pit in Germany.

facts.statement: The type locality for Mioaetus is the Hammerschmiede clay pit.
Mioaetus fossils were found in Germany.
Mioaetus was described by Mayr, Lechner, and Böhme.
Mioaetus lived during the Miocene epoch.
Mioaetus is currently considered a valid taxon.
The type species of Mioaetus is M. pforzenensis.
facts.quote: The type species is M. pforzenensis.

facts.statement: Mioaetus is classified as a member of the family Accipitridae.
facts.quote: A member of the family Accipitridae.

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus Mioaetus is M. pforzenensis.
The study describing Mioaetus was authored by Gerald Mayr, Thomas Lechner, and Madelaine Böhme.
facts.quote: Gerald Mayr, Thomas Lechner, Madelaine Böhme

facts.statement: Mioaetus fossils date to the early Late Miocene (earliest Tortonian) from southern Germany.
The environment at the Hammerschmiede site supported a productive river system that likely provided ample prey for piscivorous birds like Mioaetus.
